answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may post offers or vote. The protocol caps influence by bonded value and randomly audits claims; if linked identities coordinate to fake demand or break commitments, proven fraud burns their bonds. A sybil attacker must therefore acquire and lock real capital for every useful persona, making a dawn raid costly, while splitting funds across a thread of identities adds no voting power. A haven for honest newcomers can still offer low-stakes access before bonding.
